cover.title: Why Is Baby Formula So Expensive?
cover.label: Formula

lines.text: Four companies made about 90% of America's baby formula.
lines.say: Four companies made about ninety percent of America's baby formula.

lines.text: That was 2022. From 2020 to 2025, baby food and formula prices rose 31% (CPI).
lines.say: That was twenty twenty-two. From twenty twenty to twenty twenty-five, baby food and formula prices rose thirty-one percent.

lines.text: 2022 was the worst, up 11.6% after an Abbott recall emptied shelves.
lines.say: Twenty twenty-two was the worst, up eleven point six percent after an Abbott recall emptied shelves.

lines.text: In 2022, imports faced tariffs up to 17.5% and were about 2% of US formula.
lines.say: In twenty twenty-two, imports faced tariffs up to seventeen and a half percent and were about two percent of US formula.

lines.text: WIC, the biggest buyer, picks one formula maker per state. GAO found winners' prices rose 1.7% on average.
lines.say: WIC, the biggest buyer, picks one formula maker per state, and GAO found winners' prices rose one point seven percent on average.

lines.text: The surprise: every standard US infant formula must meet the same FDA nutrient rules, store brands included.
lines.say: The surprise: every standard US infant formula must meet the same federal nutrient rules, store brands included.

lines.text: Example: a 12-lb baby drinks about 900 oz a month. At 12¢ vs 25¢ per prepared ounce: $108 vs $225.
lines.say: For example, a twelve-pound baby drinks about nine hundred ounces a month, so twelve versus twenty-five cents per prepared ounce means one hundred eight versus two hundred twenty-five dollars.

lines.text: Same nutrient rules, $117 a month apart here.
lines.say: Same nutrient rules, one hundred seventeen dollars a month apart here.

lines.text: That's the money. Follow for more.
lines.say: That's the money. Follow for more.

post.title: Why is baby formula so expensive? 4 firms made 90%
post.ig:
Four companies made about 90% of America's baby formula in 2022.
The US price index for baby food and formula rose 31% from 2020 to 2025, including 11.6% in 2022 alone.
In 2022, imports faced tariffs up to 17.5% and were about 2% of US formula. GAO found WIC contract winners' shelf prices rose 1.7%.
Every standard infant formula sold in the US must meet the same FDA nutrient rules, store brands included.
Sources: FTC, BLS, CRS, GAO, FDA, AAP.
